In this duel to the death, you have a massive advantage by always moving first. Yet it's still not easy to win more than 1 million consistently. Just imagine how you would do in places like casinos, where you have a disadvantage. In this sense, I would call it an anti-gambling game. 

Most achievements in the game are very easy to achieve. The only two difficult achievements require accumulative winning to more than 1 million, which need some understanding about the game mechanism and a little bit of luck.

And never shoot yourself unless you are 100% certain it's a blank.

I went into a shady underground club.

The dealer placed a gun on the table, loaded randomly with blank and live rounds.
We take turns shooting off the gun at ourselves to see which rounds we got.
I leave the table as the survivor with a case full of cash.

Then I go home and play this game called "Buckshot Roulette". It's a pretty good game!

This game feels very similar to the other game done by Mike Klubnika titled "Unsorted Horror".

By that, i mean it's really really short but has an incredibly interesting and unique gameplay that makes you invested all the way to the end with 2 endings that make you question rather than feel like a victory.

I feel with Buckshot Roulette, it has an a fantastic gameplay loop which offers alot of replayability as yourself and the AI are both in a balanced role where anyone can make a simple mistake at anytime, and that makes it so much more engaging.

Highly recommend this game aswell as Unsorted Horrors for if you're looking for more of Mike's style as from the start it's very well executed.
